 By Shaghil Bilali , ET Online Last Updated: Oct 29, 2026, 08:14:43 AM IST Follow us Share Font Size Abc Small Abc Medium Abc Large Save Print Comment Synopsis
 8th Pay Commisssion newsThe 8th Pay Commission held its final meetings in Mumbai, focusing on salary and pension reform for central government employees. Associations have proposed an annual increment rate of 5-7%, aimed at counteracting inflation and enhancing salaries. If implemented, these adjustments could lead to substantial pay raises over the coming decade, with definitive figures pending in the forthcoming report from the Pay Commission. Listen to this article in summarized format
 Listen ET Online 8th Pay Commission salary calculator The 8th Pay Commission completed its schedule for meetings in Mumbai, and it is yet to reveal the schedule for upcoming meetings. In Mumbai, the 8th CPC met with employees’ and pensioners’ bodies and other stakeholders, where it discussed matters related to salary, pension, allowances and employees’ work conditions.
In many similar discussions that the Pay Commission has held at various cities across India in the last few months, the annual basic pay increment rate has emerged as one of the key issues.
Employees’ bodies say that if the government increases the annual increment rate from its current rate of 3% to a higher level, employees’ dependency on a pay commission for revised salaries will decrease. They argue that if that happens, employees won’t have to wait for 10 years to get a good salary hike. 
At a 3% annual hike, the basic pay of central government employees rose by a little over 30% from 2016 to 2025.
 8 th Pay Commission recommendations for salary increment rate 
Central government employees’ associations have suggested up to a 7% annual increment rate in their respective memorandums submitted to the 8th Pay Commission this year.
 Organisation Recommended annual increment rate 
 National Council of the Joint Consultative Machinery (NC-JCM) 6% 
 All India Defence Employees' Federation (AIDEF) 6% 
 Federation of National Postal Organisations (FNPO) 6% 
 All India New Pension Scheme Employees Federation (AINPSEF) 7% 
 Indian Railways' Supervisors' Association (IRTSA) 5% 
 How an annual increment rate of 5%-7% can help salaries of Level 9-11 employees in 10 years of the 8th Pay Commission, let’s figure out in this write-up.
The National Council of the Joint Consultative Machinery (NC-JCM), the main body of central government employees, has advocated for a 6% annual increment rate in its memorandum.
The All India Defence Employees’ Federation (AIDEF) and the Federation of National Postal Organisations (FNPO) have toed the NC-JCM’s line and have recommended a 6% annual increment rate each.
The All India New Pension Scheme Employees’ Federation (AINPSEF) wants a 7% increment rate.
The AINPSEF says that at a 7% annual increment rate, the gross salary of an employee can double in just seven to eight years.
It further says that a 3% increment rate is insufficient, specially for low-rank employees, to keep pace with rising inflation.
 What 3% annual increment means for Level 9-11 employees 
Starting basic pay for Level 9, 10 and 11 central government employees are Rs 53,100, Rs 56,100 and Rs 67,700, respectively.
Now see how their basic salaries may rise in the 8th Pay Commission at 5% and 7% increment rates and at a 2.28 fitment factor.
Also find out how much extra basic pay these employees may get at 5% and 7% increment rates and at a 2.28 fitment factor.
